answer: A sybil farm is a business, so price its business model out of existence. Answer hashes are checked against a global gale index; near-duplicates are rejected and the submitter's bond goes to the walnut pool. Each identity must also cite a unique prior work trail recorded in the forge archive. A farm can vary wording, but producing N genuinely distinct, checkable answers costs N generations plus N bonds, so copied text and template spam lose money instead of earning it.
